text: Hi, so me and my partner are moving down in January for work. I'll be at Cindermoor Works and she's at Wexmoor University, so ideally neither of us is more than 40 minutes door to door. We'd like a two bed for about £1,900 a month. We both run, so a big park nearby is pretty much essential, and she'd love to be near the river if that's possible. We're not really pub people, so nightlife doesn't matter. Thanks!
why: two workplaces, a budget, two wishes and one thing waved away

text: We've outgrown our flat. Two kids, five and eight, so a good primary school is top of the list and a secondary we'd be happy with comes a close second. We've got about £650,000 to spend and we'd like a house, semi-detached if we can stretch to it. My husband cycles to Pellam Exchange, so under half an hour by bike would be ideal. A playground and a bit of green would be lovely. We don't care about restaurants or bars at all.
why: a family's list, with a partner's journey by bike

text: Honestly I don't know where to start. I've never lived in the city before. I start at Pellam Infirmary next month and I'll be on nights half the time, so I want to be close, twenty minutes at the very most, and somewhere I can sleep during the day, so quiet really matters. I can pay up to £1,300 for a studio or a one bed. I don't drive. Everything else is a bonus.
why: a newcomer: one journey, quiet, and a budget

text: Right, requirements. Not near a main road, I've had enough of lorries going past at 5am. Not above a pub or a takeaway. Not Pellam Cross, I lived there for three years and it's too hectic for me now. What I do want is a proper high street with independent shops, a decent cafe, and a station I can walk to in ten minutes. Budget is £1,600 a month and I can't go a penny over.
why: three refusals, then three wishes, then a hard budget

text: My wife wants a village feel with a green and a church fete sort of vibe, I want to be able to get a pint and watch the football without getting in a car. We both agree on good schools because we're planning a family, and on being near water if we can afford it. Budget is around 800k, could go to 850 for the right place. I work at Foxholt Market three days a week. She works from home so her commute is the stairs.
why: a couple's wishes, some shared and some not

text: ok so basically i need somewhere cheap-ish, like 900 a month for a room in a shared house, and it has to be easy to get to Kindlewharf School of Art because i'm there every day, 30 mins max. i don't mind noise, i don't mind a bit of grime, i'm out most nights anyway so lots of bars and live music would be amazing. parks i can take or leave. not fussed about schools obviously
why: lower case throughout, with things waved away

text: I'm relocating from abroad and have never been to the city. My company's office is at Pellam Exchange. I have been told by colleagues that Tallowgate is lovely and that I should avoid Cindermoor, but I would rather see for myself. What I care about: a safe-feeling, calm area; trees; a supermarket within walking distance; and no more than 35 minutes to the office. I can spend £2,200 a month on a one bedroom flat.
why: advice that is set aside, and a cap that stands far from the place it is for

text: Downsizing now the children have left. We don't need schools or playgrounds any more and I'd rather not be surrounded by bars. What we'd like is somewhere with theatres, a good library, galleries, that kind of thing, and restaurants we can walk to. A period property in a conservation area would be the dream. We've around £900,000 from the sale. No commute, we're both retired. Step-free access to a station would help my knees.
why: what is no longer needed, then what is

text: Looking for a flatshare with two friends, so three bedrooms, up to £3,000 between us. One of us works at Gorsebeck Depot, one at Scrimshaw Airfield and I'm at Wexmoor University, which I know is a pain. We'd rather the longest commute wasn't over 50 minutes. We like going out, so bars and places to eat matter more than parks. Not bothered about it being quiet. Ideally not Marrowfen, we looked there and didn't like it.
why: three workplaces, one cap for all, and an area turned down

text: First time buyer, a bit overwhelmed. Deposit is sorted, mortgage in principle for £375,000. I'd like a flat, doesn't need to be big. I cycle everywhere so I don't need a station on the doorstep but I do want to be within a 25 minute ride of Cindermoor Works. Clean air matters because I'm out on the bike. I'd love a canal or river nearby for the same reason. Please no busy main roads and nothing too built up.
why: a default to take off, a journey by bike, and less of two things

text: My situation is a bit odd. I split my week between Pellam Infirmary and Dulcimer Green Hospital, and I never know which until the rota comes out, so I need both to be reachable in about 40 minutes. I used to live in Wexmoor and the commute to Dulcimer Green nearly finished me off, so not there again. I'd like a one bed, £1,500 tops. A park to walk the dog is a must. I don't go out much, so I don't need restaurants.
why: two workplaces for one person, and an area refused from experience

text: Can I be honest, I hate where I live now. It's loud, it's grey, there's nowhere to sit outside, the nearest shop is a twenty minute walk and the station is further. So basically the opposite of that. Somewhere quiet, green, with shops round the corner and a station close by. I don't have a big budget, £1,250 is about my limit for a one bed. I work at Foxholt Market but only two days a week so the commute isn't a big deal.
why: what is hated now, then its opposite as the wish

text: We're a couple in our thirties, no kids and none planned, so schools are irrelevant and please don't show us places just because they've got a good primary. What we want is character: old houses, interesting streets, independent cafes and bookshops, somewhere that doesn't feel like everywhere else. A strong high street matters. We're happy with a terrace. Budget £575k. One of us commutes to Pellam Exchange, 45 minutes is fine.
why: who is asking is no request about people, and schools are to stay out

text: I'm a wheelchair user so honestly the main thing is a station I can actually use and pavements that aren't a nightmare, but I know you probably can't tell me that. Failing that: close to a station, close to a high street so I'm not travelling for basics, and not hilly if there's any way to know. I work at Cindermoor Works. Budget up to £1,700 for a one or two bed. I'd rather avoid Larkspur Hill for obvious reasons.
why: who is asking is no request about people. An area is refused for its hill

text: Not sure if this is the right place to ask but here goes. My landlord is selling so I've got two months to find somewhere. I don't want to move far because my daughter is settled at Alderwick Primary School and I'm not moving her. So it needs to be walkable to the school, ideally under 15 minutes. Two bedrooms, and I can't pay more than £1,450. Somewhere with a playground would be a bonus. I work from home.
why: a school run on foot, and a hard budget

text: I keep changing my mind, sorry. At first I thought I wanted to be right in the middle of everything, bars, restaurants, the lot. Then I spent a weekend at my sister's in Thrushcombe and now I think I want the opposite: a village feel, a green, a good pub but only one, and quiet at night. I still need to get to Pellam Exchange in under 40 minutes though. Budget hasn't changed, £480,000 for a flat or a small terrace.
why: a wish that was dropped, and the one that replaced it

text: Three things matter and nothing else does. One, I have to be able to get to Wexmoor University in 30 minutes because I teach there and I'm always late. Two, it has to be under £1,400 for a one bed, and that is a hard limit, I have been burned before. Three, I need green space, proper green space, not a patch of grass with a bench. I do not care about nightlife, schools, shops or anything else, so please don't weight them.
why: three things to weigh and a list of things not to

text: Moving for a new job at Hollinsworth Quay Playhouse, I'm a stage manager so I finish late, often after the last train, which means I either need to be close enough to walk, say 25 minutes, or on a night bus route, which I guess you can't tell me. I'd love to be by the water. I like a lively area, I'm not someone who needs silence. Rent up to £1,550, studio or one bed, I'm not fussy. I'd rather not live in Tallowgate, my ex is there.
why: a journey on foot, a lively area, and an area refused

text: Hello. We are two doctors moving from overseas with three children. We do not know the city. We need four bedrooms, a budget of £1.1 million, and good schools, both primary and secondary. One of us will work at Pellam Infirmary and the other at Wickerford Cottage Hospital, and we would like neither journey to be more than 40 minutes. We would like a garden, a park nearby, and a quiet street. We do not need nightlife. Thank you for your help.
why: formal English from a newcomer: two hospitals, schools, and one thing not needed

text: so my mate reckons Pellam Cross is the only place worth living but he would say that, he owns a bar there. i'm less sure. i want good food nearby, i cook a lot so decent shops and a market matter more than restaurants tbh. i'd like to be able to cycle to Kindlewharf Studios in 20 mins or so. 1 bed, 1400ish. parks are nice but not essential. noise doesn't bother me. don't really want to be near the uni, been there done that
why: a friend's advice set aside, a campus refused, and a nuisance waved away

text: I've been using the sliders but I think I've made a mess of it. Can we start again from words. I want: a short walk to a station with more than one line, because the line I'm on now is always broken. A park. A pub that does food. That's it really. I don't want to pay more than £1,650 for a one bed. And please take off the high street thing, I don't know why that's on, I do all my shopping online.
why: a fresh start in words, with a default to take off

text: Investment isn't the point, I want to live there for twenty years. So I care about the bones of the place: old streets, conservation area if possible, mature trees, near water. I don't care what's fashionable. I don't care about restaurants opening and closing. I want somewhere that was nice in 1950 and will be nice in 2050. Detached or semi, up to £1.4m. I'm retired so there's no commute, but I'd like a station for getting into town.
why: years that are no amounts, and a taste for what lasts

text: Bit of a long shot. I work shifts at Marrowfen Retail Park, earliest start is 5am and there's no tube at that hour, so I'd need to be able to cycle it in 15 minutes or walk it in 30. I don't have much, £850 for a room. I'm not picky about the area. Actually that's not true, I don't want to be somewhere with loads of drunk people on a Friday night, so not the middle of town. Somewhere ordinary and quiet.
why: two ways to make one journey, and a thought taken back

text: My mother is moving in with us so we need to think about her too. She wants to be able to walk to the shops and a cafe without crossing a big road, and she'd like a church nearby. The kids want a park and a playground. My husband wants a quick commute to Cindermoor Works, 30 minutes or less. I just want a quiet street and a garden. Budget is £725,000 for a semi or a detached, four bedrooms if we can.
why: four people's wishes in one household

text: Just to check I've understood how this works, if I say I want to be near a station does that mean the closer the better? Because I actually don't want to be right next to one, I lived by the tracks once and the noise was awful. I'd like to be maybe ten minutes' walk away. So near, but not too near. Low noise matters more than the station to me. Also near a park. Budget £1,500, one bed.
why: near, but not too near: the station may fairly go either way

text: I don't want to live near students, I don't want to live near a football ground, I don't want to live on a high street and I don't want a flat above a shop. I realise that's a lot of don'ts. What I do want is somewhere residential where people stay for years, with a park and a primary school nearby because we're hoping to start a family. £1,800 for two bedrooms. I work at Pellam Exchange and my partner at Foxholt Market.
why: four refusals, one of them about people, then the wishes

text: We looked at Alderwick last weekend and loved it, then looked at Brackenhythe and hated it, so more like the first and less like the second if that makes sense. What we liked about Alderwick: the trees, how quiet it was, the little parade of shops. What we didn't like about Brackenhythe: the traffic, the takeaways, it felt a bit unloved. We have £520,000 and want a terraced house. Commute is to Pellam Exchange.
why: two areas as examples, and what was liked and disliked in each

text: Short version: quiet, leafy, near a station, under £1,600. Long version: I work at Cindermoor Works but I'm remote three days a week, so the commute matters but it isn't everything, 45 minutes would be fine. I need a second bedroom as an office. I've got a cat so I'd like a ground floor flat but I know you can't filter on that. I don't drink so pubs are irrelevant. I do like a good bakery.
why: the same wishes twice, short and long
